Bill.BriefDescription: Concerning emissions from certain emergency power sources.

BillBody.BillTitle: AN ACT Relating to emissions from certain emergency power sources;and adding a new section to chapter 70.94 RCW.
BillBody.EnactingClause: BE IT ENACTED BY THE LEGISLATURE OF THE STATE OF WASHINGTON:

BegSecNew.BegSecText: A new section is added to chapter 70.94 RCWto read as follows:

BillSection.RCWSLText: (1) Emergency engines or backup generators with a cumulative brakehorsepower rating greater than two thousand are in compliance for useat hospitals, sewage treatment plants, data centers, and other vitalpublic services without further state requirements if the emergencyengines: (a) Meet United States environmental protection agency emissionstandards; (b) Are fueled by ultralow sulfur diesel or ultralow sulfurbiodiesel, with a sulfur content of fifteen parts per million or 0.0015percent sulfur by weight or less; and (c) Operate a maximum of fifty hours per year for maintenance,testing, or other nonemergency use. (2) For the purposes of this section, an emergency engine means anew, dieselfueled, stationary compression ignition engine that is: p. 1 SB 5796 (a) Installed for the primary purpose of providing electrical poweror mechanical work during an emergency and is not the source of primarypower at the facility; and (b) Operated to provide electrical power or mechanical work duringan emergency under the following conditions: (i) The failure or lossof all or part of normal power service to a facility and the failure orloss of normal power service is beyond the control of the facility; or(ii) the failure or loss of all or part of a facility's internal powerdistribution system.
